title: A Case of the Mondays: Those Snaps Really Counted
seoTitle: Rams 20, Commanders 13: Puka Nacua, Myles Garrett and Those Snaps That Really Counted
summary: Rams 20, Commanders 13: Puka Nacua caught 14 balls, Myles Garrett had three sacks, the refs flagged the other team, I called the 20 for the wrong team, and UVA basketball won the day.
paragraphs: I said 20. On Friday I wrote, in public, with my name on it, that this game would be 20-17 and that I had no idea who would win. Final score: Rams 20, Commanders 13. I nailed the number. I just handed it to the wrong team. In my defense, I specifically said I couldn't tell you who it would be, and boy, did I mean that.

Here's the thing about this one. The Rams are a better team than we are, and I can live with that. What I can't live with is how we lost, which is the most Commanders way possible: to exactly two guys, both of whom we saw coming from 3,000 miles away. One on offense, one on defense. That's the whole loss. On Friday I wrote that Myles Garrett was back off IR and that Jason hoped he'd be on a snap count. Maybe he was. But those snaps REALLY counted.
## Puka Nacua, Party of One

Puka Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and the go-ahead touchdown, a leaping grab in the corner of the end zone early in the fourth quarter that broke a 13-13 tie. He was targeted 19 times. Sean McVay said afterward, "We needed all 14 of those catches," which is the nicest way a coach has ever said "we had one idea and it worked."

K'Lavon Chaisson put it more bluntly: "They threw the ball to one person all day. They ran one play all day." K'Lavon, I believe you. I watched it. Everyone watched it. The Rams told us exactly what they were going to do and then did it 14 times. Chris saw it coming at 1:22 p.m., about twenty minutes into the game: "Puka is gonna have 500 yards." Jason, an hour later: "We don't even try to cover Puka." Me, Monday morning, still not over it: "triple cover him or do SOMETHING." At some point you put four guys on him and dare Stafford to find the other ten. I'm not a defensive coordinator. I'm a man with a couch. But I'd have tried it.
## Myles Garrett Happened

Myles Garrett, playing for the first time since Week 1, had three sacks and a forced fumble. The first one was a strip-sack of Jayden late in the first half. Then center Lucas Patrick left with a concussion, and according to The Athletic, we spent the rest of the afternoon asking a sixth-round rookie to block one of the best pass rushers alive. On Friday I wrote, "So does every tackle we have." Every tackle we have is now in a support group.

Asked what happened on the fumble, Jayden said three words: "Myles Garrett happened." That is the best quote of the season and also the saddest. It's a complete postgame press conference. You could frame it. The top post on r/Commanders Sunday night was titled "This Is Why I Drink," and I'm not saying they're wrong.
## The Good Stuff, Briefly

Here's what hurts: the first half was good. Rachaad White took a screen pass 45 yards to the Rams' 7, and on the next play Jayden hit Van Jefferson, a former Ram, for a 7-yard touchdown. That was Van's first of the season, and the revenge story was all ours for about two quarters. Chaisson forced a fumble and Nick Cross fell on it. We went into halftime up 10-6, and then they retired John Riggins' 44 in front of everybody, which was the high point of my week and possibly my fall.

Then the offense went to sleep. At one point Tashan Reed had to announce, like a man reporting a rare bird sighting, that we had just picked up our first first down of the second half. Nick Cross picked off Stafford, his second takeaway of the day, and we turned it into a field goal to tie it, which JP Finlay summed up perfectly: "hard to not convert that Stafford INT into a TD." Ben Standig had it right too: "It's not that the Commanders played poorly, especially on defense." The defense was good. It just had to play the whole game with the offense handing it the ball back.

And because the football gods enjoy a theme, the Rams had their own revenge story. Emmanuel Forbes, our former first-round pick, said afterward, "Yeah I had this one circled. I was motivated to play them guys. They let me go two years ago." Chris offered a full scouting report on Monday: Forbes is "really good at reacting to the ball, it's deep balls/etc. he gets beat on." My scouting report was that he's never been a great tackler and still made a great tackle against us, because of course he did. Van Jefferson's revenge got us seven points. Forbes' revenge got them a win.
## Ref Watch: Beautiful Officiating

My one-line message to John Hussey on the [Ref Watch page](whos-reffing.html) this week was, "Be boring, John. We believe in you." John was not boring. His crew threw 16 flags, a few more than the roughly 12 a game his crews usually average. But here's the split: 10 on the Rams for 70 yards, and just six on us for 39.

On Friday I explained my entire system for watching refs: if they're flagging us, I get mad, and if they're flagging them, the officiating is beautiful. By my own system, this was some of the most beautiful officiating I've ever seen. It was gorgeous. We lost anyway. The one flag that really hurt was blocking in the back on a punt return late in the fourth, which pushed us back to our own 11. Ref Watch updates Tuesday with whoever has us at the Giants, so I can start getting mad in advance.
## Three Seconds

Let's talk about the end, because I've been thinking about it since 4:12 Sunday afternoon. Down seven, 52 seconds left, no timeouts, starting at our own 11. Jayden hit Stefon Diggs for 41 yards and spiked it at midfield. A few plays later we had the ball at the Rams' 31 with three seconds left. One play. Thirty-one yards from the end zone. And Jayden threw it short to Chig Okonkwo, and then the laterals started, and it died like every lateral play in human history.

Dan Quinn said the play had a check: the first read is the end zone, but if the defense brings an all-out blitz, you throw it short. The Rams showed the blitz and then only sent five. Jayden said they were expecting it. Pro Football Talk said the team still has "a little too much Backward Hat Energy," which is the most devastating thing anyone wrote about us all weekend. Jason, Sunday night, made the case better than anybody: "Put the ball in the end zone. And hope for the best." He added that he knows the odds of a Hail Mary are very low, but the odds of the lateral stuff are even lower. Jason is right. We have literally done this before. Against the Bears. With this exact quarterback. It worked.
## The Group Chat

Jason's week went like this. Friday: "I'm assuming a loss." Sunday at 10 a.m.: "I do have a feeling we play well today." He was right. We played well. We lost. At 4:17: "Me. I hate everything." And then, Monday morning, from a place of hard-won peace: "I don't really get mad anymore when I just know other teams players are better. Like the Rams are a better team. But I just still get so frustrated with general football incompetence." I've been trying to say that sentence my whole life.

Chris spent part of the game in his bathroom, which, it turns out, has a TV he had never once turned on before. He was installing a bidet. He also, on Sunday afternoon, said what every fan in America was yelling at fourth and inches: "Dude. 4th and less than 1. Go for it." By Monday he'd moved on to roster construction: "We gotta go full Indy," sell anybody with value who isn't Jayden. Then, one message later: "except we dont really have anyone other teams want." That's the whole Commanders trade deadline in two texts.
!photo chris-bathroom

And the biggest news from the chat: Chris bought the MacBook Air. Last week his entire pregame take was whether he needed the Pro or if the Air was okay, and I told him the Air was one million percent fine. He got the Air. He's setting it up now. Of all the predictions I made this week, it's the only one that came in.
## The Undercard: Basketball Season
UVA football had a bye this week and finished it undefeated. That's the best result the football program has had in a month, and I'm choosing to celebrate it.

Meanwhile, about 10 miles down the road from Northwest Stadium, No. 9 Virginia basketball beat No. 12 Arkansas 91-72 on Sunday at Capital One Arena. The Hoos led by 27 in the second half, all five starters scored in double figures, and Johann Grünloh was the game's MVP with 15 points and five blocks. It was the biggest margin UVA has ever beaten a ranked non-conference team by. John Calipari said afterward, "They're a top-10 team, maybe even better." So on Sunday, the best team in the DC area played in Chinatown, not Landover. UVA is 3-0 and hosts Bucknell Tuesday night. I'd like to formally request that Ryan Odom be consulted on any future three-second plays.
## Call Your Shot

Every single one of you picked us to win. The crowd's median pick was 24-20, which means you also nailed the 20, and you also gave it to the wrong team. I've never been prouder of this community. CryoGen came closest at 24-20, off by 11, and BT called 27-21.

As for me, I never picked a winner, so technically I couldn't lose. I'm still in first place on the [season leaderboard](leaderboard.html) at 1-2, off by 6.7 a game, just ahead of Taylor P. This is my strategy now. I will never pick a winner again, and I'm going to ride it all the way to a championship. The Giants poll is open. Come take it from me.
## Next Up

It's a short week. We're at the Giants on Thursday night, they're 5-2-1, and we're 2-5-1 and three games back. Jayden said it plainly: "Next week is a must-win." JP Finlay said it even more plainly: "Win Thursday and they're 2 games back in the division with 8 to play. Lose and it's curtains. If it's not curtains already." The trade deadline is Tuesday, so by the time we kick off, the roster may look different, or, given Chris's analysis, exactly the same.

Here's the hope part, because there's always a hope part. We're on life support, but the NFC East is still the NFC East. Garrett doesn't play for the Giants. Puka doesn't play for the Giants. Give me a reason, boys. Thursday. Hail.

wireTaps: Thursday at the Giants: must-win, or is it already curtains?

chris-bathroom.caption: Chris's bathroom, published with his permission. Note the TV he had never turned on before Sunday, and note what is on the screen: a flag. You can't escape Ref Watch. Not even in there.
